items.summary: AR(1) recursion a_{k+1} = alpha a_k + eta_k with sigma_eta^2 = 1-alpha^2.
items.note: Definition of the chain; ch05a_g_recursion confirms the defining relation holds definitionally.

items.summary: Standing assumptions a_0 ~ N(0,1), a_0 independent of the innovations, |alpha| < 1.
items.note: A list of standing hypotheses has no truth value on its own, so what is proved is that they are jointly realisable, for every chain length L and every alpha with |alpha| < 1: ch05a_epsLaw is the explicit product measure on R^L whose coordinates are independent (ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun for the product measure), whose 0th marginal is exactly gaussianReal 0 1 (= a_0 ~ N(0,1)) and whose every later marginal is exactly gaussianReal 0 sigma_eta^2 (= eta_k iid N(0,sigma_eta^2)); and ch05a_sigEta2_pos proves |alpha| < 1 => sigma_eta^2 = 1-alpha^2 > 0, so the prescribed variance is a legitimate one. Previously skipped as 'not an identity'.

items.summary: a_1 = alpha a_0 + eta_0.
a_2 = alpha^2 a_0 + alpha eta_0 + eta_1.
a_3 = alpha^3 a_0 + alpha^2 eta_0 + alpha eta_1 + eta_2.
a_k = alpha^k a_0 + sum_{j=0}^{k-1} alpha^{k-1-j} eta_j.
items.note: Proved by induction for all k from the recursion; the natural-number subtraction k-1-j is handled by omega side conditions.

items.summary: The induction step alpha(alpha^k a_0 + sum) + eta_k = alpha^{k+1} a_0 + sum_{j<=k} alpha^{k-j} eta_j.
epsilon = (a_0, eta_0, ..., eta_{L-2})^T, the vector of independent atoms.
items.note: Definition.

items.summary: a = G_alpha epsilon for a deterministic lower-triangular G_alpha.
items.note: General L, no longer L = 4. (G_alpha)_{ij} = alpha^{i-j} for j <= i and 0 otherwise; ch05a_G_lower_triangular gives lower-triangularity for every n, and ch05a_g_linear_map proves sum_j (G_alpha)_{ij} eps_j = a_i for every n and every row i : Fin n. The proof truncates the row sum to j <= i (Finset.sum_subset), peels off the a_0 term with Finset.sum_range_succ' and closes against the unrolled representation ch05a_g_unroll.

Encoded as the conditional-mean recursion m_{k+1} = alpha m_k (innovations are centred); proved by induction.

[FIDELITY NOTE 2026-09-13] Status kept as 'proved', scope narrowed. ch05a_condmean is the audit's own recursion (0 |-> a0, k+1 |-> alpha * condmean k) and ch05a_g_memory proves only that its closed form is alpha^k a_0. The probabilistic content of the display -- that the conditional mean obeys m_{k+1} = alpha m_k BECAUSE every innovation has zero mean -- is put in by hand in the definition and is never connected to ch05a_ar1.

a_k = alpha^{k-j} a_j + sum_{r=j}^{k-1} alpha^{k-1-r} eta_r for j <= k.
Cov(a_j,a_k) = alpha^{k-j} Var(a_j) = alpha^{k-j}.

The reindexing i = k-1-j is exactly Finset.sum_range_reflect.

[FIDELITY NOTE 2026-09-13] Status kept as 'proved', claim narrowed. The tex is a two-step chain; ch05a_g_var_sum states only the SECOND equality, the reindexing i = k-1-j (Finset.sum_range_reflect). The first, probabilistic step 'Var(a_k) = alpha^{2k} Var(a_0) + sigma_eta^2 sum ...' (variances of independent terms add) is not in the statement at all: nothing in the theorem mentions ch05a_var or ch05a_gcov or any variance. Read the item as an identity between the two displayed right-hand expressions, not as a variance computation.

items.summary: sum_{i=0}^{k-1} (alpha^2)^i = (1-alpha^{2k})/(1-alpha^2).
items.note: Requires alpha^2 != 1, as the text states.

items.summary: alpha^{2k} + (1-alpha^2)(1-alpha^{2k})/(1-alpha^2) = 1.

items.note: Proved by induction on d for all k, d.

items.note: Proved for all k,d from the atom-coefficient representation, using sum_range_reflect and the geometric sum; the entrywise form is ch05a_noname24.

items.summary: N(a_0;0,1) prod_k N(a_{k+1}; alpha a_k, sigma_eta^2) = N(a; 0, Sigma_0).
items.note: General L >= 2, no longer L = 2; normalisation included. The engine is the bidiagonal factorisation Sigma_0 = G D G^T and Q_0 = B^T D^{-1} B with B = I - alpha S the differencing matrix and D = diag(1, sigma_eta^2, ...): it gives the exponent (ch05a_g_quadform_general: a^T Q_0 a = a_0^2 + (1/sigma_eta^2) sum (a_{k+1}-alpha a_k)^2) and the normalisation (ch05a_Sig0_det: det Sigma_0 = (sigma_eta^2)^{L-1}) at once. ch05a_g_P0_general states it with Q_0; ch05a_g_P0_general_inv rewrites Q_0 as (Sigma_0)^{-1} via ch05a_g_Q0_general so the right-hand side is literally N(a; 0, Sigma_0). Hypotheses: L >= 2 (the displayed product over k = 0..L-2 is empty at L = 1) and sigma_eta^2 > 0, which is the chapter's standing |alpha| < 1.

items.summary: The explicit dense symmetric Toeplitz display of Sigma_0.
items.note: Sigma_0 defined entrywise as alpha^{Nat.dist i j}; ch05a_g_Sig0_matrix checks the displayed literal matrix at L = 4 with symbolic alpha.
Proved as a matrix inverse (Matrix.inv_eq_right_inv) with symbolic alpha under 1-alpha^2 != 0.
Proved as a matrix inverse with symbolic alpha; confirms both the exactly-zero corner and the extra alpha^2 on the interior diagonal.

items.summary: Q_0 = Sigma_0^{-1} is tridiagonal with 1/s at the ends, (1+a^2)/s inside and -a/s off-diagonal.
items.note: General L >= 2, no longer L = 2,3,4,5. Proved as a genuine matrix inverse: ch05a_Sig0_factor gives Sigma_0 = G D G^T, ch05a_Q0_factor gives Q_0 = B^T D^{-1} B, and ch05a_B_mul_G / ch05a_G_mul_B prove B = G^{-1} for every n; multiplying out gives Q_0 Sigma_0 = I and hence (Sigma_0)^{-1} = Q_0 by Matrix.inv_eq_left_inv. The displayed entries (1/sigma_eta^2 at the ends, (1+alpha^2)/sigma_eta^2 inside, -alpha/sigma_eta^2 off-diagonal, exact 0 at distance >= 2) are the definition of ch05a_Q0 and were already proved entrywise for all n. L >= 2 is needed and is not a trivialisation: at L = 1 the displayed matrix is (1/sigma_eta^2), which is not the inverse of Sigma_0 = (1).

items.summary: Entrywise description of Q_0 (diagonal cases and off-diagonal -alpha/sigma_eta^2, zero beyond).
items.note: This display is the definition of Q_0; the individual entry claims are proved for all n in ch05a_g_precision_interior, ch05a_g_precision_offdiag, ch05a_g_precision_distant_zero, ch05a_noname17, ch05a_noname19.
Definition of the centred Gaussian density in precision form; sanity lemma ch05a_g_gaussian_precision_pos shows it is strictly positive when det Sigma_0 > 0.

items.note: Proved for all L from the density definition via log_mul / log_rpow / log_exp.

items.summary: P_0(a) = p(a_0) prod_k p(a_{k+1} | a_k).
items.note: Definition of the Markov factorisation; ch05a_P0_factorised_pos gives positivity.

items.note: The transition and prior laws; encoded as the one-dimensional Gaussian density ch05a_gauss used inside ch05a_P0_factorised.

items.note: Proved for all chain lengths, with the constant computed explicitly as (m+1) log(2 pi) + m log sigma_eta^2 where m = L-1.

items.summary: Expanding the square: (a_{k+1}-alpha a_k)^2 = a_{k+1}^2 - 2 alpha a_k a_{k+1} + alpha^2 a_k^2 inside the sum.
a^T Q a = sum_m Q_mm a_m^2 + 2 sum_{m<n} Q_mn a_m a_n for symmetric Q.
items.note: General L, no longer L = 3,4, with a fully symbolic symmetric Q. Proof is the entrywise argument: expand a . (Q a) as a double sum, split each row into its diagonal term and Finset.univ.erase i, split the erased part into the i < j and j < i halves, and fold the second half onto the first with Finset.sum_comm' plus the symmetry hypothesis.

items.summary: The only products of distinct coordinates are -(2 alpha/sigma_eta^2) sum_k a_k a_{k+1}.
items.note: Proved for all chain lengths as a Finset identity.

items.note: Proved for all n and all index pairs at distance 1 (so both orders).

items.note: Proved for all n.

(Q_0)_{mm} = (1+alpha^2)/sigma_eta^2 for 1 <= m <= L-2.
items.note: Proved for all n for every interior index.

items.note: Both equalities proved; the second is exactly where sigma_eta^2 + alpha^2 = 1 is used.

items.note: Encoded as the factorisation criterion for the conditional density: with all other coordinates fixed, the Gaussian kernel exp(-(1/2)(q11 x^2 + 2 q12 x y + q22 y^2 + b1 x + b2 y)) satisfies f(x,y) f(0,0) = f(x,0) f(0,y) for all x,y iff q12 = 0. Both directions proved.

items.summary: -log P(a) = -log p(a_0) - sum_k log p(a_{k+1}|a_k) for any first-order Markov density.

items.lean_name: ch05a_g_markov_hessian_sparsity_general (general form; supersedes the vacuous ch05a_g_markov_hessian_sparsity), ch05a_g_markov_hessian_sparsity_dist, ch05a_chain_separable
items.summary: d^2[-log P]/da_i da_j = 0 for |i-j| >= 2.
items.note:
General L and general potentials, no longer the two-function instance. For an arbitrary first-order Markov negative log-density -log P(a) = f_0(a_0) + sum_k f_k(a_k, a_{k+1}) (arbitrary f_0 and f_k, no smoothness assumed) and any i, j with |i-j| >= 2 in either order, the mixed second partial vanishes identically. The mechanism is proved, not assumed: ch05a_chain_separable shows that no summand contains both coordinates, so as a function of (a_i, a_j) the density splits additively as g(a_i) + h(a_j), and an additively separable function has zero mixed derivative. Coordinates are perturbed with Function.update, and the j < i case is reduced to the i < j one by Function.update_comm.

[FIDELITY NOTE 2026-09-13] The cited witness was corrected. The original lean_name ch05a_g_markov_hessian_sparsity is vacuous: 'deriv (fun z => deriv (fun x => g x + h z) x0) z0 = 0' assumes the additive separability g(x) + h(z) that is the whole content of the thesis claim, and the inner derivative is literally independent of z, so the conclusion holds by deriv_const. The faithful general statement does exist in the file -- ch05a_g_markov_hessian_sparsity_general (hij : i + 2 <= j), proved for all m via ch05a_chain_separable -- and the record now points at the general form (ch05a_g_markov_hessian_sparsity_dist). Status 'proved' therefore stands on the general theorem, not the trivial one.

items.summary: E[a_k | a_{\k}] = -(Q_kk)^{-1} sum_{l != k} Q_kl a_l.
items.note:
[REPAIRED 2026-09-14] Re-proved after the 2026-09-13 fidelity downgrade; both gaps named there are now closed, and the result holds at arbitrary size n (no fixed L).

MAIN (ch05a_g_gaussian_cond_precision): for Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R with Q.IsSymm and 0 < Q k k, any a : Fin n -> R, any x,
  Function.update a k x <dot> Q *v (Function.update a k x)
    = Q k k * (x - m)^2 + ch05a_condMin Q a k,   m := ch05a_condMean Q a k = -(Q k k)^{-1} * sum_{l in univ.erase k} Q k l * a l.
That is: the section of the genuine quadratic form a . Q.mulVec a in coordinate k is EXACTLY the square completed about the displayed right-hand side. The expansion is a separate entrywise lemma (ch05a_g_quadratic_form_section): Matrix.mulVec_apply_eq_sum to get the double sum, Finset.add_sum_erase to split both sums at index k, Finset.sum_add_distrib, then Finset.sum_congr to match the row-k and column-k cross sums using Matrix.IsSymm.apply.

This closes gap 1 of the downgrade (the objective is no longer written by hand -- it is the k-section of a . Q.mulVec a) and gap 2 (symmetry is now hypothesised). Neither hypothesis trivialises the claim: without symmetry the linear coefficient of the section is sum_{l!=k}(Q_kl + Q_lk) a_l and the displayed formula is FALSE; 0 < Q k k is what makes the section bounded below. ch05a_g_gaussian_cond_precision_posDef derives both from Q.PosDef (Matrix.isHermitian_iff_isSymm, Matrix.PosDef.diag_pos), which is what a precision matrix is.

COROLLARIES proved from the identity: ch05a_g_gaussian_cond_precision_min (m minimises the form); ..._min_strict (uniquely -- every x != m strictly increases it); ..._density (there is c > 0 with exp(-(1/2) * section x) = c * ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDFReal m <(Q k k)^{-1}> x for all x, i.e. the k-section of the Gaussian weight is the N(m, (Q_kk)^{-1}) density up to a positive constant); ..._mean (mathlib's ProbabilityTheory.integral_id_gaussianReal at exactly those parameters: the mean of that law is the displayed right-hand side).

NOT FORMALISED (the remaining encoding convention, stated so it is not misread): no probability space, no Gaussian random vector on R^n and no MeasureTheory.condExp object is constructed, so E[a_k | a_{\k}] is not a formal conditional expectation in this file. Taken as given are (i) that the joint density of the centred Gaussian is proportional to exp(-(1/2) a^T Q a) and (ii) that the conditional law of coordinate k given the rest is the renormalised k-section of that density. Granting (i)-(ii), the Lean content above is exactly the display: the section is proportional to the N(m, (Q_kk)^{-1}) density, whose mean is m. Scope note: Q here is a general symmetric matrix, not specifically the tridiagonal Q0 of eq:g-Q0.

items.note: Definition.

items.summary: Q_0 is local and tridiagonal, but after diffusion and marginalisation Q_t is generally nonlocal and dense.
items.note: General L >= 3, no longer the single instance L = 3, alpha = 1/2, e^{-2t} = 1/2. Both halves of the boxed display are stated together for every L >= 3, every alpha with 0 < |alpha| < 1 and every t > 0: (i) (Sigma_0)^{-1} = Q_0 and every entry of Q_0 at distance >= 2 is exactly zero (local and tridiagonal); (ii) Sigma_t is invertible (ch05a_Sigt_det_ne_zero) and Q_t = Sigma_t^{-1} has a nonzero entry at distance >= 2, located in the first column. The mechanism is a Green's-function identity: if the first column of a right inverse of Sigma_t were supported on rows 0 and 1, rows 1 and 2 of Sigma_t Q = I would force Sigma_t,10 Sigma_t,21 = Sigma_t,11 Sigma_t,20, i.e. e^{-2t} alpha^2 (e^{-2t} - 1) = 0, impossible for alpha != 0 and t > 0. SCOPE CAVEAT, stated so the status is not read as more than it is: what is proved at general L is the loss of locality (at least one exact zero of Q_0 at distance >= 2 becomes nonzero in Q_t), not the literal reading of the word 'dense' as 'every entry of Q_t is nonzero'. Full density is verified only at the L = 3 instance (ch05a_g_locality_loss_summary), where the exact inverse is computed and its (0,2) entry is -1/14 != 0.
